title: fix: report canonical route url for hidden prefix slash route
body:
#### Checklist

- [x] run `npm run unit -- test/route-prefix.test.js`
- [x] run `npm run lint:eslint -- lib/route.js test/route-prefix.test.js`

#### Description of change

When a `/` route is registered under a prefix with `prefixTrailingSlash: 'both'`, Fastify registers a hidden trailing-slash route for matching `/prefix/` but only exposes `/prefix` through `onRoute`.

This updates the request route metadata for that hidden route so `request.routeOptions.url` also reports the canonical `/prefix` value. Non-prefix routes that intentionally include a trailing slash keep reporting their own route URL.

Fixes #4424
author: paulkagiri

linked_issues.title: routerPath returns url with a trailing slash
linked_issues.body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [X] I have searched existing issues to ensure the issue has not already been raised


### Issue

Originally this error comes from [fastify-metrics](https://github.com/SkeLLLa/fastify-metrics) plugin. It relies on two things: 
 - `onRoute` hook to set up a metric for the route;
 - request `routerPath` property to find the route metric from the request context.
 
 The problem happens when you use a plugin prefix with the `prefixTrailingSlash` option set to `both` (default) value. In this case, the `onRoute` hook will be called only once, so `fastify-metrics` will set up only one route, but internally there are two different routes with two different `routerPath` properties. So `fastify-metrics` will not record metrics for requests with trailing slash.
 
 Example:
 ```js
 'use strict'

const fastify = require('fastify')()

fastify.addHook('onRoute', ({ method, url }) => {
  console.log('New route added:', method, url)
})

fastify.register(async (fastify) => {
  fastify.get('/', async (request) => {
    console.log(request.routerPath)
  })
}, { prefix: '/foo' })

fastify.ready(() => {
  fastify.inject({ method: 'GET', url: '/foo' })
  fastify.inject({ method: 'GET', url: '/foo/' })
})
 ```
 
 Output:
 ```js
 New route added: GET /foo
New route added: HEAD /foo
New route added: HEAD /foo/
/foo
/foo/
 ```
 
 If we don't call `onRoute` twice, that means that we want to hide the second route from a user. So from the user's perspective, there should be only one route. If it's true, then we should return `routerPath` with a trimmed trailing slash.
